summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study gave 12 healthy young Japanese men a single 2,000 FU oral dose of nattokinase (NSK-SD) versus placebo and tracked coagulation/fibrinolysis markers over 8 hours. Nattokinase significantly increased D-dimer and FDP, prolonged aPTT, decreased Factor VIII activity, and increased antithrombin compared with baseline/placebo (all p<0.05 for most measures), while other measured parameters showed no significant between-group differences. Findings support acute pro-fibrinolytic/anticoagulant effects of nattokinase, though exact effect magnitudes, CIs and per-arm SDs for most endpoints are only available graphically (Fig. 2) rather than in text/tables.

summary: In this single-blind RCT of 61 subacute ischemic stroke patients in Vietnam, adding oral Nattospes (a nattokinase-containing nutraceutical, 300 FU/capsule, 4 capsules/day) to standard-of-care rehabilitation (electroacupuncture plus IV Naatrapyl) for 60 days was compared to placebo plus the same standard of care. summary: This 90-day randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 178 patients with stable coronary artery disease tested nattokinase (NK), red yeast rice (RYR), their combination (NK+RYR), or placebo. The combined NK+RYR supplementation produced the largest improvements in triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, diastolic blood pressure, LDH, and anticoagulation markers (increased antithrombin III, decreased thromboxane B2) compared with placebo (most comparisons p<0.01), while NK or RYR alone showed more limited, marker-specific benefits; no adverse events were attributed to the interventions.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: TXB2, 6-keto-PGF1α, and AT-III per-arm/per-timepoint numeric values (means/SDs) are reported only in Figure 2A/2B, not in text or tables, so arm_results for outcomes 11-13 are marked not_reported per rule 10; only the between-group p-values stated in text were extractable. summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial in 43 Korean adults (healthy or with metabolic syndrome) tested oral Ultra Nattokinase® 600 mg/day for 4 weeks versus placebo, measuring changes in coagulation markers (FDP, fibrinogen) rather than clinical cardiovascular endpoints. FDP increased with nattokinase relative to placebo in the full ITT analysis, but the treatment-effect difference was not statistically significant (p=0.0583); it reached significance only after excluding subjects with vitamin K or alcohol intake (p=0.0468). A companion rat plasma experiment showed dose-dependent inhibition of collagen-induced platelet aggregation, supporting an antithrombotic mechanism, but the human trial itself found no clinically definitive cardiovascular benefit.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This paper studies coagulation/fibrinolytic biomarkers (FDP, fibrinogen) in healthy/metabolic-syndrome subjects, not classic CVD prevention endpoints (BP, lipids, MACE) — mapped to symptom_domain 'fibrinolytic_biomarkers'/'coagulation_platelet_function'. Design is a 2-period, 2-sequence (NP/PN) crossover; only period-1 (pre-crossover) means are unconfounded by carryover and are extracted as the primary arm_results; period-2 values exist in the tables but mix sequences and were not separately extracted to avoid conflating carryover with treatment effect — noted as a limitation. Age (mean/SD) was not reported anywhere in the text. BMI not reported. Fig. 2 rat dose-response data (5,10,50,100 mg/mL inhibition ratios) given as text values, not a clinical outcome, so only baseline (0 mg/mL, arm_id=2 proxy) and highest dose (100 mg/mL, arm_id=1 proxy) extracted illustratively as outcome_id=6; intermediate rat doses (5, 10, 50 mg/mL) omitted since they don't map to the two clinical arms — full data: 5mg/mL=69%(2.8% inhib), 10mg/mL=62%(12.7% inhib), 50mg/mL=16%(77.5% inhib). Fibrinogen full-population (not just male subgroup) per-arm means/SDs were not given in text, only the p-value (0.4326) for comparison — so only the male subgroup change values were extractable numerically. No CIs reported anywhere in paper, only means±SD and p-values. Higher_is_better set to true for FDP because the paper interprets increased FDP after nattokinase as evidence of enhanced fibrinolytic activity (their hypothesized beneficial mechanism), not as a marker of pathological clot breakdown/bleeding risk — this is a nonstandard interpretation worth flagging for meta-analysis synthesis. Baseline demographics only report sex counts/percentages per arm; no age or BMI given.
